name: Chassékerk
description: The Chassékerk, Karel Petrus Tholens's former Roman Catholic Church of Our Lady of Perpetual Help, was built in 1924-26 on Chasséstraat in a style influenced by the Amsterdam School: large plain brick surfaces, a broad column-free nave with narrow aisles under one great roof, and two slender towers flanking a porch of round arches. Closed in 1998 and nearly demolished, it was saved by neighbourhood opposition and now houses Chassé Dance Studios, a ballet school and a hotel in the old rectory.
funFact: Squatters occupied the church in 2004, and after the housing corporation's demolition plans were dropped, its crypt was dug out in the 2010s to make one of the largest cellars in an existing Amsterdam building.
